item.title: Oil slicks seen from space: the devastating impact of boat strikes on fragile Gulf ecosystems
item.description:
Since the US war on Iran began in February, there have been hundreds of oil spills, posing a ‘generational’ threat to wildlife

The vast, dark slicks in the strait of Hormuz are visible from space. Throughout October, oil tankers were struck by missiles or sea mines in the waterway and spilled crude into the sea. The pollution has spread across the Gulf, contaminating coastlines and threatening to cause lasting damage to marine ecosystems that are home to dolphins, sea turtles and countless species of fish.

Eight months into the war between the US and Iran, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping routes has become a battlefield and the centre of a growing environmental disaster.

item.title: Top Iranian official warns military bases from 'West Asia to Europe' would be targeted if US renews attacks
item.description:
Top Iranian official warns military bases from 'West Asia to Europe' would be targeted if US renews attacks

Iran’s top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned that Tehran could strike military bases involved in any renewed US attacks against Iran.

"If the US launches another war against Iran, every military base involved in the aggression - from West Asia to Europe - will be a legitimate target for Iran’s lethal strikes," Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said in a post on X.

"NO SAFE DISTANCE. NO SAFE HAVEN. NO IMMUNITY," he added.

item.title: Double amputee marathon runner criticises Badenoch for ‘weaponising his success’
item.description:
Paralympian Richard Whitehead ‘gobsmacked’ at Tory leader’s speech over proposed £36bn welfare cuts

The double amputee marathon runner Richard Whitehead has criticised Kemi Badenoch for “weaponising his sporting success” to justify her proposed £36bn welfare cuts.

The Conservative leader used the example of “double amputees running marathons” in a speech this week to explain the reasoning behind her proposed cuts to disability benefits, which she said were enabling people to “live a life of dependency”.

item.title: ‘The world we know is over’ without urgent climate action, leaders tell Cop31
item.description:
Marshall Islands president warns of worsening floods as UN chief calls for a windfall tax on oil and gas firms

Failure to provide an overwhelming response to the climate crisis means “the world we know is over”, the president of the embattled Marshall Islands has warned, as dozens of leaders gathered in Turkey for the Cop31 climate summit.

Hilda Heine, one of a handful of Pacific Island leaders to make an impassioned speech at Cop31 on Wednesday, told other heads of state that overshooting the 1.5C Paris temperature target would mean waves eating away their shores and floods that destroy towns, schools and hospitals.
